title: Design a Governed Analytics + Cortex Platform (Data Architect)

teaser.setup: You're the data architect. The business wants natural-language analytics and an AI assistant over the warehouse — without data leaving governance, and without the bill exploding. Design it on Snowflake and defend the calls.
you_will_practice: RBAC, masking, and row-access enforced through AI
Query performance and cost control under challenge

sample_node.prompt: Why keep the GenAI inside Snowflake (Cortex) instead of calling an external LLM?
sample_node.model: Data never leaves the governance boundary, so existing RBAC, masking, and row-access policies still apply and there's no egress/compliance headache. Cortex functions/agents run where the data lives. Trade-off: you're bounded by Cortex's model catalog and features — for a capability it lacks (e.g. a specific external model or long multi-turn chat) you'd route out through a governed gateway with masking, accepting the added control burden.
signals: names when you'd still go external + the trade-off

n1.prompt: Clarify first, then give your one-paragraph design for NL analytics + an AI assistant over the warehouse.
n1.model: Clarify: data sensitivity (PII/regulated?), who can see what, freshness needs, query volume/concurrency, and the cost ceiling. Design: governed warehouse (layered raw→clean→marts), a semantic model for NL→metrics, Cortex Analyst/Search for in-boundary AI, RBAC + masking + row-access enforced under every query, read-only least-privilege roles for the assistant, and cost guardrails. Verify generated SQL; cite the rows.

n2.prompt: How do you ingest and keep the data fresh enough for the assistant to be trusted?
n2.model: Layered pipeline (raw → cleaned → marts) with incremental loads (streams/CDC or scheduled merges), tracked freshness/lag SLOs per table, and provenance so an answer can cite when the data was last updated. Full rebuilds only as a safety net. Surface freshness to the assistant so it can say 'as of <timestamp>'. Stale data silently wrong is worse than a visible lag.

n3.prompt: Why keep the GenAI inside Snowflake (Cortex) instead of calling an external LLM?
n3.model: Data never leaves the governance boundary, so existing RBAC/masking/row-access apply and there's no egress/compliance issue. Cortex runs where the data lives. Trade-off: bounded by Cortex's model catalog/features — for something it lacks you'd route out through a governed gateway with masking, accepting extra control burden.
signals: names when you'd still go external

n4.prompt: How do you guarantee the assistant can't show a user data they aren't allowed to see?
n4.model: Run the assistant's queries under the user's identity/role, not a superuser service account, so RBAC + row-access policies + dynamic masking apply automatically — you can't return what the role can't select. Never post-filter in the app. Audit every query. For shared service patterns, pass the user context into row-access policy conditions. Access control lives in the warehouse, not the prompt.
signals: queries run as the user's role, not superuser

n5.prompt: NL→SQL can generate a wrong or dangerous query. How do you make it safe and correct?
n5.model: Prefer a governed semantic model (Cortex Analyst) over free text-to-SQL so the AI maps to vetted metrics/joins, not arbitrary SQL. Read-only least-privilege role (no writes/DDL). Validate/whitelist generated SQL, cap scanned bytes, and show the SQL + cite the result rows so a wrong number is auditable. Treat 'the AI wrote a wrong number' as a validation + provenance problem, not an accept-on-faith one.
signals: show SQL + cite rows + scan cap

n6.prompt: A dashboard that was fast is now slow after 10× data growth. Diagnose on Snowflake.
n6.model: Read the Query Profile. Common causes: poor partition pruning (cluster on the filtered/join columns), spilling to disk (warehouse undersized for the step), exploding joins from a grain/key bug, or scanning columns you discard. Fix the specific cause — clustering for pruning, right-size the warehouse for spill, fix the join grain. Snowflake has no b-tree indexes, so 'add an index' is the wrong instinct; pruning + clustering + warehouse sizing are the levers.

n7.prompt: Finance says the Snowflake + Cortex bill doubled this month. Walk your response.
n7.model: Find the delta by warehouse/query/workload before acting. Usual suspects: a Cortex job inferring over millions of un-pre-filtered rows, an auto-resume warehouse left running, or a new large scan. Fix: filter with cheap SQL BEFORE inference, route to a smaller Cortex model where adequate, batch via scheduled jobs, cache/persist results, right-size + auto-suspend warehouses. Add resource monitors + budget alerts so it's visible before the invoice.
signals: find the delta by workload first

n8.prompt: What do you ship first, and what do you deliberately not promise?
n8.model: Ship a governed vertical slice: one high-value subject area with a semantic model, Cortex Analyst read-only under user roles, freshness + cost guardrails, and citations on answers. Don't promise: 100% correct NL→SQL on every question, sub-second on unbounded scans before load-testing, or write/action capability early. Trade a fake guarantee for a measurable one: 'vetted metrics, cited rows, an accuracy number you can hold me to.'

n9.prompt: Where did you assert a choice without the mechanism, the trade-off, or the verification?
checklist: I enforced access via the user's role, not the app
I preferred a semantic model over raw text-to-SQL
I diagnosed perf via the Query Profile (pruning/spill/grain)
I found cost by workload and pre-filtered before inference
I scoped an honest first slice and refused fake guarantees

recommend.label: Keep Asking Why — data platform chain
